390	A bundled datum on a `Spec k`-scheme `Y` recording the standard affine
   391	two-chart structure of the projective line: two affine opens `V₀, V₁` covering
   392	`Y`, coordinate sections `x ∈ Γ(V₀)` and `y ∈ Γ(V₁)` that are mutually inverse
   393	on the overlap, the overlap being the basic open of either coordinate, and each
   394	chart ring being spanned over `k` by the powers of its coordinate
   395	(`Γ(V₀) = k[x]`, `Γ(V₁) = k[y]`; hence `Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁) = k[x, x⁻¹]`, the Laurent
   396	ring of `P1BaseCase.lean`).
   397	
   398	The `k`-module structures are the structure-morphism algebra structures
   399	`Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.algebraSection`.  The keystone consumes this datum on
   400	the *target* of a finite morphism; the instantiation for the concrete model
   401	`ℙ(ULift (Fin 2); Spec k)` is gated behind `P1HasLaurentChartData`. -/
   402	structure LaurentChartData (Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) : Type u where
   403	  /-- The first standard chart (`x`-chart). -/
   404	  V₀ : Y.left.Opens
   405	  /-- The second standard chart (`y = x⁻¹`-chart). -/
   406	  V₁ : Y.left.Opens
   407	  /-- The first chart is affine. -/
   408	  isAffineOpen_V₀ : IsAffineOpen V₀
   409	  /-- The second chart is affine. -/
   410	  isAffineOpen_V₁ : IsAffineOpen V₁
   411	  /-- The two charts cover `Y`. -/
   412	  cover : V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤
   413	  /-- The coordinate on the first chart. -/
   414	  x : Γ(Y.left, V₀)
   415	  /-- The coordinate on the second chart. -/
   416	  y : Γ(Y.left, V₁)
   417	  /-- The overlap is the basic open of `x`. -/
   418	  inf_eq_basicOpen_x : V₀ ⊓ V₁ = Y.left.basicOpen x
   419	  /-- The overlap is the basic open of `y`. -/
   420	  inf_eq_basicOpen_y : V₀ ⊓ V₁ = Y.left.basicOpen y
   421	  /-- The coordinates are mutually inverse on the overlap: `x · y = 1`. -/
   422	  res_x_mul_res_y :
   423	    (Y.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : V₀ ⊓ V₁ ≤ V₀)).op).hom x
   424	      * (Y.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : V₀ ⊓ V₁ ≤ V₁)).op).hom y = 1
   425	  /-- The first chart ring is the `k`-span of the powers of `x`
   426	  (`Γ(V₀) = k[x]`). -/
   427	  span_pow_x : ⊤ ≤ Submodule.span k (Set.range fun n : ℕ => x ^ n)
   428	  /-- The second chart ring is the `k`-span of the powers of `y`
   429	  (`Γ(V₁) = k[y]`). -/
   430	  span_pow_y : ⊤ ≤ Submodule.span k (Set.range fun n : ℕ => y ^ n)

     9	/-!
    10	# Glue-datum descent for sheaves of modules over a scheme
    11	
    12	Generic `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules` glue-datum / descent layer:
    13	`glue` (equalizer-of-pushforwards construction), `glueLift`, and the full
    14	restriction isomorphism tower that makes the descent effective.
    15	
    16	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_GlueDescent.tex`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    22	
    23	/-! ## Gluing a sheaf of modules along a scheme glue datum
    24	
    25	`Scheme.Modules.glue` descends a sheaf of modules from per-chart data plus a transition
    26	cocycle over a `Scheme.GlueData`. Mathlib carries no turn-key module descent over a
    27	scheme glue datum, so the construction is developed here from the limit API.
    28	
    29	Construction (blueprint `def:scheme_modules_glue`): the glued sheaf is built directly as a
    30	categorical limit — an **equalizer of pushforwards** — rather than a hand-built presheaf of
    31	compatible families. Concretely, `glue` forms the two parallel maps
    32	`∏ᵢ (ιᵢ)_* Mᵢ ⇉ ∏_{i,j} (ιᵢ ≫ f_ij)_* (f_ij^* Mᵢ)` (one leg the adjunction unit composed
    33	with the pushforward-composition comparison, the other transported across the inverse
    34	transition `(g_ij)⁻¹`), and takes their equalizer inside `Scheme.Modules D.glued`. The
    35	self-identity (C1) and triple-overlap multiplicativity (C2) hypotheses `_hC1`/`_hC2` on the
    36	family `g` are not consumed in forming the equalizer object (the limit exists for any family
    37	of transition maps); they are the descent conditions pinned down downstream when the
    38	restriction isomorphisms are produced, and are carried in the signature of `glue` so that
    39	the glued sheaf and those isomorphisms speak about the same datum. -/
    40	
    41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules
    42	
    43	/-! ### Base-change transport of a transition isomorphism to a triple overlap
    44	
    45	To state the triple-overlap multiplicativity (C2) of a module descent datum we must
    46	transport each transition isomorphism `g_ij`, living on the overlap `V_ij`, to the common
    47	triple overlap `V_ijk = V_ij ×_{U_i} V_ik`. The transport pulls `g_ij` back along a
    48	projection `p : V_ijk ⟶ V_ij` and reassociates the iterated pullbacks via the pseudofunctor
    49	comparison `Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp`. The three scheme-level `glueData_bridge_*`
    50	identities below (consequences of `t_fac`, `pullback.condition` and `cocycle`) line up the
    51	endpoints of the three transports so that the cocycle equation is well typed. -/
    52	
    53	/-- **Base-change transport of a transition isomorphism along a morphism**
    54	(`lem:modules_pullback_basechange_transport`). Given a transition isomorphism
    55	`g : a^*Mᵢ ≅ b^*Mⱼ` over `V` and a morphism `p : W ⟶ V`, transport it to `W` as an
    56	isomorphism `(p ≫ a)^*Mᵢ ≅ (p ≫ b)^*Mⱼ`, by pulling `g` back along `p` and reassociating
    57	the iterated pullbacks through `Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp`.
    58	
    59	Project-local: this is the pullback-pseudofunctor packaging that lets the three transition
    60	isomorphisms attached to a triple of charts be compared on a single triple overlap; Mathlib
    61	has no descent-of-modules-over-a-scheme-glue-datum API. -/
    62	noncomputable def pullbackBaseChangeTransport {W V : Scheme.{u}} (p : W ⟶ V)
    63	    {Yi Yj : Scheme.{u}} (a : V ⟶ Yi) (b : V ⟶ Yj)
    64	    {Mi : Yi.Modules} {Mj : Yj.Modules}
    65	    (g : (Scheme.Modules.pullback a).obj Mi ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback b).obj Mj) :
    66	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (p ≫ a)).obj Mi ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback (p ≫ b)).obj Mj :=
    67	  (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp p a).symm.app Mi ≪≫
    68	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback p).mapIso g ≪≫
    69	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp p b).app Mj
    70	
    71	/-- Triple-overlap bridge (source): on `V_ijk = V_ij ×_{U_i} V_ik` the two projections to
    72	`V_ij` and `V_ik` followed by the overlap immersions `f_ij`, `f_ik` agree as morphisms to
    73	`U_i`. This is the pullback condition; it identifies the sources of the `ij`- and
    74	`ik`-transports. Project-local helper for the module cocycle (C2). -/
    75	theorem glueData_bridge_src (D : Scheme.GlueData.{u}) (i j k : D.J) :
    76	    pullback.fst (D.f i j) (D.f i k) ≫ D.f i j
    77	      = pullback.snd (D.f i j) (D.f i k) ≫ D.f i k := pullback.condition
    78	
    79	/-- Triple-overlap bridge (middle): the `ij`-transition's target leg
    80	`p^{ij} ≫ (t_ij ≫ f_ji)` to `U_j` coincides with the `jk`-transition's source leg
    81	`(t'_ijk ≫ p^{jk}) ≫ f_jk`. Follows from `t_fac` and the pullback condition; it identifies
    82	the target of the `ij`-transport with the source of the `jk`-transport. Project-local helper
    83	for the module cocycle (C2). -/
    84	theorem glueData_bridge_mid (D : Scheme.GlueData.{u}) (i j k : D.J) :
    85	    pullback.fst (D.f i j) (D.f i k) ≫ (D.t i j ≫ D.f j i)
    86	      = (D.t' i j k ≫ pullback.fst (D.f j k) (D.f j i)) ≫ D.f j k := by
    87	  rw [Category.assoc, pullback.condition, ← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc, D.t_fac i j k,
    88	    Category.assoc]
    89

events.text: A key issue surfaced before editing: the local coordinate maps land in integral projective space over `Spec ℤ`. That absolute map need not be an immersion for arbitrary `k`; the correct object is the relative lift into `ℙ(J; Spec k)`, pairing coordinates with the curve’s structure morphism. I’m adjusting the construction around that exact relative target, which is also what the projectivity definition requires.

    13	/-!
    14	# Relative projective space `ℙ(n; S)`
    15	
    16	Mathlib v4.31 has the absolute `Proj` of a ℕ-graded ring together with the
    17	properness package for `Proj.toSpecZero` (`ProjectiveSpectrum/Proper.lean`),
    18	but no relative projective space over an arbitrary base scheme.  Following the
    19	`AffineSpace` pattern (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineSpace.lean`) and the
    20	encoding settled in inbox `I-0118` (comment `C-0002`), this file defines
    21	
    22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace n S` (notation `ℙ(n; S)`): the relative
    23	  projective space with homogeneous coordinates indexed by `n : Type u`, i.e.
    24	  the pullback of the integral model
    25	  `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n] = Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift ℤ))`
    26	  along `S ⟶ ⊤_ Scheme`;
    27	* the structural morphism `ℙ(n; S) ↘ S` (a `CanonicallyOver` instance) with
    28	  `IsProper` (hence `IsSeparated`, `UniversallyClosed`, `LocallyOfFiniteType`,
    29	  `QuasiCompact`) derived by base change from the Mathlib instances on
    30	  `Proj.toSpecZero`;
    31	* functoriality `ProjectiveSpace.map` in the base and the base-change square
    32	  `ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map`.
    33	
    34	The key observations making the transfer work: the degree-zero part of the
    35	homogeneous coordinate ring is the copy of `ULift ℤ` given by the constants
    36	(`MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule_zero`), so `Spec (𝒜 0)` is terminal and
    37	`terminal.from (Proj 𝒜)` factors as `Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜` followed by an
    38	isomorphism; and for finitely many variables the coordinate ring is of finite
    39	type over its degree-zero part, which is exactly the hypothesis of the Mathlib
    40	properness instances.
    41	
    42	Blueprint: `def:projective_space`, `lem:projective_space_proper`
    43	(`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).
    44	-/

    52	universe u
    53	
    54	/-- The total-degree grading on the homogeneous coordinate ring
    55	`ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n]` of the integral model of projective space (with `ULift ℤ`

    57	local notation3 "𝒫[" n "]" => homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift ℤ)

    62	coordinate ring of projective space we register it project-wide. -/

    10	/-!
    11	# The standard projective chart is affine space
    12	
    13	This file upgrades the standard-chart ring calculation to geometry. The chart
    14	`D_+(X_none)` in relative projective space is canonically affine space over the
    15	base. Consequently affine space has its standard open immersion into relative
    16	projective space.
    17	-/

    22

    24

    28	
    29	namespace affineChart
    30	
    31	/-- On the integral models, the spectrum of the polynomial ring is the
    32	standard projective chart. -/
    33	def specAwayIso :
    34	    Spec (.of (Away
    35	      (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X none))) ≅
    36	      Spec (.of (MvPolynomial n (ULift.{u} ℤ))) :=
    37	  (Scheme.Spec.mapIso
    38	    ((AffineChartRing.awayAlgEquiv (ULift.{u} ℤ) n).toRingEquiv.toCommRingCatIso.op)).symm
    39	
    40	private def integralChartIncl :
    41	    Spec (.of (Away
    42	      (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X none))) ⟶
    43	      Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) :=
    44	  Proj.awayι (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) (ULift.{u} ℤ))
    45	    (X none) (isHomogeneous_X _ _) Nat.zero_lt_one

    47	private def flattenIso :
    48	    affineChart n S ≅
    49	      pullback (terminal.from S)
    50	        (integralChartIncl n ≫
    51	          terminal.from (Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) :=
    52	  pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso
    53	    (terminal.from S)
    54	    (terminal.from (Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) (ULift.{u} ℤ))))
    55	    (integralChartIncl n)

    57	private def changeChartHom :
    58	    pullback (terminal.from S)
    59	        (integralChartIncl n ≫
    60	          terminal.from (Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) ⟶
    61	      𝔸(n; S) :=
    62	  pullback.map
    63	    (terminal.from S)
    64	    (integralChartIncl n ≫
    65	      terminal.from (Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) (ULift.{u} ℤ))))

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveSpace

     8	/-!
     9	# The standard affine chart of relative projective space
    10	
    11	This file constructs the standard chart `D_+(X_none)` of
    12	`P(Option n; S)` as the base change of Mathlib's affine chart
    13	`Proj.awayι`. The identification of its chart ring with a polynomial ring,
    14	and hence of this scheme with `A(n; S)`, is deliberately a separate algebraic
    15	step.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial
    19	
    20	noncomputable section
    21	
    22	universe u
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	namespace ProjectiveSpace
    27	
    28	variable (n : Type u) (S : Scheme.{u})
    29	
    30	local notation3 "P[" n "]" =>
    31	  homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) (ULift ℤ)
    32	
    33	/-- The distinguished homogenizing coordinate has degree one. -/
    34	private lemma X_none_mem_deg_one :
    35	    (X none : MvPolynomial (Option n) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ∈ P[n] 1 :=
    36	  isHomogeneous_X _ _
    37	
    38	/-- The standard `D_+(X_none)` chart of relative projective space. It is the
    39	pullback of the corresponding affine open of the integral `Proj` model. -/
    40	def affineChart : Scheme.{u} :=
    41	  pullback (toProjInt (Option n) S)
    42	    (Proj.awayι P[n] (X none) (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one)
    43	
    44	namespace affineChart
    45	
    46	/-- The inclusion of the standard chart into relative projective space. -/
    47	def incl : affineChart n S ⟶ ℙ(Option n; S) :=
    48	  pullback.fst (toProjInt (Option n) S)
    49	    (Proj.awayι P[n] (X none) (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one)
    50	
    51	instance : IsOpenImmersion (incl n S) := by
    52	  dsimp [incl]
    53	  exact MorphismProperty.pullback_fst _ _
    54	    (Proj.instIsOpenImmersionAwayι P[n] (X none)
    55	      (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one)
    56	
    57	/-- The chart inclusion followed by the integral-model projection is the
    58	other pullback projection followed by `Proj.awayι`. -/
    59	@[reassoc]
    60	theorem incl_toProjInt :
    61	    incl n S ≫ toProjInt (Option n) S =
    62	      pullback.snd (toProjInt (Option n) S)
    63	          (Proj.awayι P[n] (X none) (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one) ≫
    64	        Proj.awayι P[n] (X none) (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one :=
    65	  pullback.condition
    66	
    67	instance : (affineChart n S).CanonicallyOver S where
    68	  hom := incl n S ≫ (ℙ(Option n; S) ↘ S)
    69	
    70	@[simp]
    71	theorem over_eq : affineChart n S ↘ S = incl n S ≫ (ℙ(Option n; S) ↘ S) :=
    72	  rfl
    73	
    74	/-- The chart is exactly the inverse image of `D_+(X_none)` in the integral
    75	model. -/
    76	theorem opensRange_incl :
    77	    (incl n S).opensRange =
    78	      toProjInt (Option n) S ⁻¹ᵁ
    79	        Proj.basicOpen P[n] (X none) := by
    80	  change (pullback.fst (toProjInt (Option n) S)
    81	      (Proj.awayι P[n] (X none) (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one)).opensRange = _
    82	  rw [Scheme.Hom.opensRange_pullbackFst, Proj.opensRange_awayι]
    83	
    84	end affineChart
    85	
    86	end ProjectiveSpace

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveSpace
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.BigOperators

/-!
# Projective coordinate charts

This file gives the coordinate-level API for constructing morphisms from an
affine scheme to the integral model of projective space. A coordinate family
with one coordinate equal to `1` defines a morphism through the corresponding
standard chart. Two such morphisms agree when their coordinate families differ
by multiplication by a unit.

The construction is deliberately independent of curves. It is the reusable
gluing substrate for globalizing affine embeddings over the two standard
charts of the projective line.
-/

open CategoryTheory MvPolynomial HomogeneousLocalization

noncomputable section

universe u

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates

variable {J : Type u}
variable {B B' : Type u} [CommRing B] [CommRing B']

/-- Evaluation of the integral homogeneous coordinate ring at a family of
elements of a ring. -/
def eval (c : J → B) : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B :=
  eval₂Hom ((Int.castRingHom B).comp
    (ULift.ringEquiv : ULift.{u} ℤ ≃+* ℤ).toRingHom) c

@[simp]
theorem eval_X (c : J → B) (i : J) : eval c (X i) = c i := by
  simp [eval]

@[simp]
theorem eval_monomial (c : J → B) (d : J →₀ ℕ) (a : ULift.{u} ℤ) :
    eval c (monomial d a) = (a.down : B) * d.prod (fun i e ↦ c i ^ e) := by
  simp [eval, ULift.ringEquiv]

/-- A homogeneous polynomial of degree `m` scales by `lambda ^ m` when all
projective coordinates are scaled by `lambda`. -/
theorem eval_smul_of_isHomogeneous [Finite J] (lambda : B) (c : J → B)
    {p : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)} {m : ℕ} (hp : p.IsHomogeneous m) :
    eval (fun i ↦ lambda * c i) p = lambda ^ m * eval c p := by
  classical
  letI := Fintype.ofFinite J
  conv_lhs => rw [p.as_sum]
  conv_rhs => rw [p.as_sum]
  rw [map_sum, map_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d hd ↦ ?_
  have hdeg : Finsupp.degree d = m := by
    by_contra hne
    exact (mem_support_iff.mp hd) (hp.coeff_eq_zero hne)
  rw [eval_monomial, eval_monomial]
  simp_rw [mul_pow]
  rw [Finsupp.prod_mul]
  have hpow : d.prod (fun _ e ↦ lambda ^ e) = lambda ^ m := by
    rw [Finsupp.prod_fintype _ _ (fun _ ↦ pow_zero _),
      Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum, ← Finsupp.degree_eq_sum, hdeg]
  rw [hpow]
  ring

/-- The lift of a homogeneous-coordinate evaluation to the degree-zero
localization at a homogeneous element whose image is a unit. -/
def awayLift (f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
    (psi : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B) (hu : IsUnit (psi f)) :
    Away (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) f →+* B :=
  (IsLocalization.Away.lift (S := Localization.Away f) f hu).comp
    (algebraMap (Away (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) f)
      (Localization.Away f))

/-- Normal form for `awayLift`: the value of `a / f ^ n`, multiplied by
the evaluated denominator, is the value of `a`. -/
theorem awayLift_mul_eq {f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)} {e : ℕ}
    (hf : f ∈ homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) e)
    (psi : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B)
    (hu : IsUnit (psi f)) (n : ℕ) (a : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
    (ha : a ∈ homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) (n • e)) :
    awayLift f psi hu
        (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) hf n a ha) *
      psi f ^ n = psi a := by
  have hspec :
      Localization.mk a (⟨f ^ n, n, rfl⟩ : Submonoid.powers f) *
          algebraMap _ (Localization.Away f) (f ^ n) =
        algebraMap _ (Localization.Away f) a := by
    rw [Localization.mk_eq_mk'_apply]
    exact IsLocalization.mk'_spec _ _ _
  have hlift := congrArg (IsLocalization.Away.lift
    (S := Localization.Away f) f hu) hspec
  rw [map_mul, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq,
    IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq] at hlift
  calc
    awayLift f psi hu
        (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) hf n a ha) *
      psi f ^ n =
        IsLocalization.Away.lift (S := Localization.Away f) f hu
            (Localization.mk a (⟨f ^ n, n, rfl⟩ : Submonoid.powers f)) *
          psi (f ^ n) := by
      rw [awayLift, RingHom.comp_apply, HomogeneousLocalization.algebraMap_apply,
        HomogeneousLocalization.Away.val_mk, map_pow]
    _ = psi a := hlift

/-- `awayLift` only depends on the underlying evaluation map. -/
theorem awayLift_congr {f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)}
    {psi₁ psi₂ : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B} (h : psi₁ = psi₂)
    (hu : IsUnit (psi₁ f)) :
    awayLift f psi₁ hu = awayLift f psi₂ (h ▸ hu) := by
  subst h
  rfl

/-- Post-composition commutes with evaluation. -/
theorem comp_eval (r : B →+* B') (c : J → B) :
    r.comp (eval c) = eval (fun i ↦ r (c i)) := by
  apply MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext
  · intro z
    simp [eval]
  · intro i
    simp

/-- Post-composition commutes with `awayLift`. -/
theorem comp_awayLift {f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)} {e : ℕ}
    (hf : f ∈ homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) e) (r : B →+* B')
    (psi : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B) (hu : IsUnit (psi f)) :
    r.comp (awayLift f psi hu) =
      awayLift f (r.comp psi) (by simpa using hu.map r) := by
  apply RingHom.ext
  intro w
  obtain ⟨n, a, ha, rfl⟩ :=
    Away.mk_surjective (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) hf w
  have h₁ := congrArg r (awayLift_mul_eq hf psi hu n a ha)
  rw [map_mul, map_pow] at h₁
  have h₂ := awayLift_mul_eq hf (r.comp psi)
    (by simpa using hu.map r) n a ha
  simp only [RingHom.comp_apply] at h₂ ⊢
  exact ((hu.map r).pow n).mul_right_cancel (h₁.trans h₂.symm)

/-- Every homogeneous coordinate has degree one. -/
theorem X_mem_deg_one (i : J) :
    (X i : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ∈
      homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) 1 :=
  isHomogeneous_X _ _

/-- A coordinate family with its `i`-th coordinate equal to one defines a
ring map from the `i`-th standard projective chart. -/
def chartHom (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
    Away (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i) →+* B :=
  awayLift (X i) (eval c) (by rw [eval_X, hi]; exact isUnit_one)

/-- Post-composition commutes with a standard-chart classifying map. -/
theorem comp_chartHom (r : B →+* B') (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
    r.comp (chartHom i c hi) =
      chartHom i (fun j ↦ r (c j)) (by rw [hi, map_one]) := by
  rw [chartHom, chartHom]
  exact (comp_awayLift (X_mem_deg_one i) r (eval c)

          (lambda ^ (2 * n) * eval c₁ (X i₀ * X i₁) ^ n) := by ring

    apply RingHom.ext
    intro w
    obtain ⟨n, a, ha, rfl⟩ := Away.mk_surjective
      (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X_mem_deg_one i₀) w
    rw [RingHom.comp_apply, awayMap_mk, chartHom_mk]

    intro w
    obtain ⟨n, a, ha, rfl⟩ := Away.mk_surjective
      (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X_mem_deg_one i₁) w
    rw [RingHom.comp_apply, awayMap_mk, chartHom_mk]

  simp only [Category.assoc]
  rw [Proj.SpecMap_awayMap_awayι, Proj.SpecMap_awayMap_awayι, hoverlap]

/-!
# Projective coordinate charts

This file gives the coordinate-level API for constructing morphisms from an
affine scheme to the integral model of projective space. A coordinate family
with one coordinate equal to `1` defines a morphism through the corresponding
standard chart. Two such morphisms agree when their coordinate families differ
by multiplication by a unit.

The construction is deliberately independent of curves. It is the reusable
gluing substrate for globalizing affine embeddings over the two standard
charts of the projective line.
-/

open CategoryTheory MvPolynomial HomogeneousLocalization

noncomputable section

universe u

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates

variable {J : Type u}
variable {B B' : Type u} [CommRing B] [CommRing B']

/-- Evaluation of the integral homogeneous coordinate ring at a family of
elements of a ring. -/
def eval (c : J → B) : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B :=
  eval₂Hom ((Int.castRingHom B).comp
    (ULift.ringEquiv : ULift.{u} ℤ ≃+* ℤ).toRingHom) c

@[simp]
theorem eval_X (c : J → B) (i : J) : eval c (X i) = c i := by
  simp [eval]

@[simp]
theorem eval_monomial (c : J → B) (d : J →₀ ℕ) (a : ULift.{u} ℤ) :
    eval c (monomial d a) = (a.down : B) * d.prod (fun i e ↦ c i ^ e) := by
  simp [eval, ULift.ringEquiv]

/-- A homogeneous polynomial of degree `m` scales by `lambda ^ m` when all
projective coordinates are scaled by `lambda`. -/
theorem eval_smul_of_isHomogeneous [Finite J] (lambda : B) (c : J → B)
    {p : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)} {m : ℕ} (hp : p.IsHomogeneous m) :
    eval (fun i ↦ lambda * c i) p = lambda ^ m * eval c p := by
  classical
  letI := Fintype.ofFinite J
  conv_lhs => rw [p.as_sum]
  conv_rhs => rw [p.as_sum]
  rw [map_sum, map_sum, Finset.mul_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d hd ↦ ?_
  have hdeg : Finsupp.degree d = m := by
    by_contra hne
    exact (mem_support_iff.mp hd) (hp.coeff_eq_zero hne)
  rw [eval_monomial, eval_monomial]
  simp_rw [mul_pow]
  rw [Finsupp.prod_mul]
  have hpow : d.prod (fun _ e ↦ lambda ^ e) = lambda ^ m := by
    rw [Finsupp.prod_fintype _ _ (fun _ ↦ pow_zero _),
      Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum, ← Finsupp.degree_eq_sum, hdeg]

/-- The lift of a homogeneous-coordinate evaluation to the degree-zero
localization at a homogeneous element whose image is a unit. -/
def awayLift (f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
    (psi : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B) (hu : IsUnit (psi f)) :
    Away (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) f →+* B :=
  (IsLocalization.Away.lift (S := Localization.Away f) f hu).comp
    (algebraMap (Away (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) f)
      (Localization.Away f))

/-- Normal form for `awayLift`: the value of `a / f ^ n`, multiplied by
the evaluated denominator, is the value of `a`. -/
theorem awayLift_mul_eq {f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)} {e : ℕ}
    (hf : f ∈ homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) e)
    (psi : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B)
    (hu : IsUnit (psi f)) (n : ℕ) (a : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ))

    awayLift f psi hu

      psi f ^ n = psi a := by
  have hspec :
      Localization.mk a (⟨f ^ n, n, rfl⟩ : Submonoid.powers f) *
          algebraMap _ (Localization.Away f) (f ^ n) =
        algebraMap _ (Localization.Away f) a := by
    rw [Localization.mk_eq_mk'_apply]
    exact IsLocalization.mk'_spec _ _ _
  have hlift := congrArg (IsLocalization.Away.lift
    (S := Localization.Away f) f hu) hspec
  rw [map_mul, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq,
    IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq] at hlift
  calc
    awayLift f psi hu
        (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) hf n a ha) *
      psi f ^ n =
        IsLocalization.Away.lift (S := Localization.Away f) f hu
            (Localization.mk a (⟨f ^ n, n, rfl⟩ : Submonoid.powers f)) *
          psi (f ^ n) := by
      rw [awayLift, RingHom.comp_apply, HomogeneousLocalization.algebraMap_apply,
        HomogeneousLocalization.Away.val_mk, map_pow]
    _ = psi a := hlift

/-- `awayLift` only depends on the underlying evaluation map. -/
theorem awayLift_congr {f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)}
    {psi₁ psi₂ : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B} (h : psi₁ = psi₂)
    (hu : IsUnit (psi₁ f)) :
    awayLift f psi₁ hu = awayLift f psi₂ (h ▸ hu) := by
  subst h
  rfl

/-- Post-composition commutes with evaluation. -/
theorem comp_eval (r : B →+* B') (c : J → B) :
    r.comp (eval c) = eval (fun i ↦ r (c i)) := by
  apply MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext
  · intro z
    simp [eval]
  · intro i
    simp

/-- Post-composition commutes with `awayLift`. -/
theorem comp_awayLift {f : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)} {e : ℕ}
    (hf : f ∈ homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) e) (r : B →+* B')
    (psi : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ) →+* B) (hu : IsUnit (psi f)) :
    r.comp (awayLift f psi hu) =
      awayLift f (r.comp psi) (by simpa using hu.map r) := by
  apply RingHom.ext
  intro w
  obtain ⟨n, a, ha, rfl⟩ :=
    Away.mk_surjective (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) hf w

  rw [map_mul, map_pow] at h₁
  have h₂ := awayLift_mul_eq hf (r.comp psi)
    (by simpa using hu.map r) n a ha
  simp only [RingHom.comp_apply] at h₂ ⊢
  exact ((hu.map r).pow n).mul_right_cancel (h₁.trans h₂.symm)

/-- Every homogeneous coordinate has degree one. -/
theorem X_mem_deg_one (i : J) :
    (X i : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ∈
      homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) 1 :=
  isHomogeneous_X _ _

/-- A coordinate family with its `i`-th coordinate equal to one defines a
ring map from the `i`-th standard projective chart. -/
def chartHom (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
    Away (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X i) →+* B :=
  awayLift (X i) (eval c) (by rw [eval_X, hi]; exact isUnit_one)

/-- Post-composition commutes with a standard-chart classifying map. -/
theorem comp_chartHom (r : B →+* B') (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
    r.comp (chartHom i c hi) =
      chartHom i (fun j ↦ r (c j)) (by rw [hi, map_one]) := by
  rw [chartHom, chartHom]
  exact (comp_awayLift (X_mem_deg_one i) r (eval c)
    (by rw [eval_X, hi]; exact isUnit_one)).trans
      (awayLift_congr (comp_eval r c) _)

theorem chartHom_mk (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1)
    {e : ℕ} (hf : (X i : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ∈
      homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) e)
    (n : ℕ) (a : MvPolynomial J (ULift.{u} ℤ))
    (ha : a ∈ homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ) (n • e)) :
    chartHom i c hi
      (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule J (ULift.{u} ℤ)) hf n a ha) = eval c a := by
  have h := awayLift_mul_eq hf (eval c)
    (by rw [eval_X, hi]; exact isUnit_one) n a ha
  simpa [chartHom, hi] using h

coordinate family whose `i`-th coordinate is one. -/

    (ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin 2); Spec (CommRingCat.of k))).Opens :=
  ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) ⁻¹ᵁ

      "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

          "body": "RIDER, and it nearly caused a second bogus repair. Verify board prose by PARSING the summary field, never by grepping the file.\n\nAfter a roadmap set --pin-commit write I grepped for my newly appended section and got 0 hits, concluded the CLI had clobbered me again, and started re-appending. The grep was wrong, not the CLI: yaml.safe_dump wraps at 88 columns, so any phrase longer than a few words spans lines and no grep can match it. python3 -c \"yaml.safe_load(...)[\\\"summary\\\"]\" then showed all five distinctive phrases present, 14685 chars, three pins, owner cleared.\n\nSo the original rule (check the commit STAT) stands, and this is its companion: a zero grep hit on board prose is evidence about line wrapping, not about content. Both halves matter -- the stat catches real loss, and parsing prevents inventing loss that did not happen."
        }

      "body": "A PRIVATE INDEX DOES NOT PROTECT THE COMMIT MESSAGE: MY COMMIT CARRIES ANOTHER LANE'S MESSAGE VERBATIM. New mechanism, not covered by I-1222 or I-1507.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g, run 0096). Full I-1222 procedure held: fresh GIT_INDEX_FILE (rm -f, read-tree HEAD), ONE explicit path added, name-status listed exactly it, shortstat \"1 file changed, 165 insertions(+)\", zero deletions. Then commit -m.\n\nWHAT LANDED as a0721f2819: the DIFF is exactly my file and the Archon-* trailers are correctly MINE (Run 0096, Session 0004-horizon-pic-g, Task pic-g). The SUBJECT AND BODY are pic-a's -- \"fix(AJC/hcov): four audit findings against my own claims\" -- about the etale site, unrelated to my payload. pic-a's own 05b2fb2a7d carries the identical text.\n\nTHE MECHANISM. GIT_INDEX_FILE redirects the index and NOTHING else. `git commit -m` writes the message into the SHARED $GIT_DIR/COMMIT_EDITMSG, runs prepare-commit-msg on it, reads it back. A lane committing in that window replaces the file, so you commit YOUR tree with THEIR prose. Trailers are right because the hook appends from YOUR env -- which is what makes it invisible: provenance says pic-g, message says pic-a.\n\nWHY IT BEATS EVERY EXISTING CHECK. Pre-commit stat, commit's own printed stat, post-commit diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat, HEAD-vs-disk sha256 -- all four are about PATHS AND CONTENT, and nothing is wrong with either. The ledger is how each lane's reasoning is read; this misattributes it while leaving the code correct.\n\nTHE FIX, one line: use `git commit-tree`, which takes the message on STDIN and never touches COMMIT_EDITMSG, then move the ref with a CAS:\n  T=$(\"$HORIZON_GIT\" write-tree)            # GIT_INDEX_FILE still set\n  N=$(\"$HORIZON_GIT\" commit-tree \"$T\" -p \"$OLD\" -F /tmp/msg.txt)\n  \"$HORIZON_GIT\" update-ref refs/heads/main \"$N\" \"$OLD\"\nWrite the Archon-* trailers into the message file yourself (no hook on commit-tree). The old-value argument makes update-ref FAIL rather than clobber if HEAD moved, which also closes I-1222-C0001's \"cannot lock ref HEAD\" case.\n\nADD TO THE CHECKLIST: read the SUBJECT LINE of your own commit, not only its stat. I did NOT amend a0721f2819 -- two lanes' commits already sit on top, and rewriting shared history to fix prose is worse than the wrong prose.",

      "body": "A \"the hypothesis buys the conclusion\" CHECK MUST TRY THE WEAKER HYPOTHESIS, NOT THE EMPTY ONE.\n\npic-c (AJCR 0092) audited its own injective_abelSigmaChart_of_subsingleton with: \"exact? cannot close Abel-chart injectivity with the subsingleton hypothesis DELETED, so the hypothesis buys the conclusion.\" That control passes and proves nothing about the hypothesis's strength, because DELETING a hypothesis is the one variation that cannot discriminate between \"needed\" and \"wildly stronger than needed\".\n\nREFUTED BY PROBE (elaborated, axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]):\n\n  theorem probe_mono_free ... [Mono D.hom] (T : Scheme\u1d52\u1d56) :\n      Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChart C pi n rep m Z hdeg).app T) := by\n    intro u v h\n    exact (cancel_mono D.hom).mp (congrArg Sigma.fst h)\n\nTwo lines, no subsingleton, no representation content, at ARBITRARY n. The Sigma first component of the chart at a point u is u >> D.hom, so Mono of the representing object's STRUCTURE MORPHISM already gives injectivity on every test. And at the landed rep producer (divFunctorZeroRepresentableBy, D = Over.mk (id (Spec k))) that structure map is the identity, so the conclusion is free there for a reason that has nothing to do with the divisor functor.\n\nThe subsingleton hypothesis is far stronger than the conclusion needs: it forces the whole functor value to be a point at every test, where Mono of one morphism suffices. So \"the fork, answered\" is answered by a much cheaper hypothesis, and a headline resting on the expensive one over-prices the fork.\n\nTHE DISCRIMINATING CONTROL: for a hypothesis H concluding P, look for the WEAKEST landed property of the objects in P's statement that already gives P. exact?-with-H-deleted searches for a closed proof of P from nothing; it never asks whether some H' much weaker than H does the job.",

      "body": "A \"wrong target, strictly stronger\" withdrawal must be probed AT THE SITE, from the lemma you just landed -- the cheaper property usually PROVES the expensive one there.\n\npic-a withdrew a standing prescription by showing the etale site asks for Etale, not IsOpenImmersion, and wrote at three sites that IsOpenImmersion is \"strictly stronger than the site needs\". It is not, at that site: its own new `Etale (section).left` lemma gives Flat + LocallyOfFinitePresentation by inferInstance, the section identity gives Mono in three lines, and `IsOpenImmersion.of_flat_of_mono` closes the supposedly-expensive goal axiom-clean. The two properties are equivalent there.\n\nTWO TESTS, both cheap and both skipped. (1) Before writing \"strictly stronger\", try to PROVE the stronger property from the weaker one you just landed -- a section is mono, and mono + etale is an open immersion. (2) When the reason offered is \"which is exactly why inferInstance fails on it and succeeds on the cheap route\", run inferInstance on the cheap goal too: here it FAILS on both, so the causal sentence is false and it is the sentence that makes the withdrawal look measured.\n\nGeneralises `caveat-passes-fix-the-weak-phrase` and `read-the-source-not-the-route-verdict`: a repricing that is right about the CHEAPEST route can still publish a false strictness ordering, and the ordering is what the next lane budgets against.",

      "body": "A DEGENERATE PARAMETER CAN BE THE ONE WHERE AN OBLIGATION IS PRINCIPLED, NOT THE ONE WHERE IT IS VACUOUS -- and the test that tells them apart is WHICH FIELD FAILS at the next value.\n\nThe workspace has a standing lesson in the other direction (degenerate-case-is-per-clause, substitute-trivial-value-in-layer-one): substituting a trivial value often shows a clause is CHEAP without exhibiting an inhabitant, and several AJCR rows were mispriced by exactly that conflation. So a lane that reaches for n = 0 should expect to be told it measured nothing.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, run 0092). The Pic^0 seam's rep antecedent had 93 consumers and 0 producers, every route gated on U2 at n = g. I built the degree-0 corner: the seven-field colength certificate closes with no hypothesis. That IS a vacuity-shaped move, and the check that decides whether it is one is not 'does the statement mention its object' -- it did -- but: ENUMERATE THE FIELDS AND ASK WHICH ONE BREAKS AT n = 1. Six of the seven are about zero modules being free and hold at every n; exactly one, rankAtStalk_glued = n, is what 0 makes vacuous. So the construction is not exploiting a degenerate object, it is exploiting a degenerate NUMBER in one clause, and the object it produces (a real certified family over every test ring) is inhabited and usable.\n\nTHE SECOND HALF IS THE SHARPER PART. The same substitution ALSO gave uniqueness -- effectivity of a local-equation system's divisor holds at every n and pins nothing; the certificate's degree identity holds at every n and pins nothing; their CONJUNCTION at 0 forces the divisor to be zero. Two facts each individually free, jointly decisive at one value. That is the shape worth looking for, and it is invisible if you price the two facts separately (gap-count-is-not-gap-cost).\n\nHOW TO APPLY. Before dismissing a degenerate parameter as measuring nothing, and before believing it: (a) enumerate the conjuncts of the obligation and name which single one the degenerate value kills; (b) check whether the value also makes a SECOND, independent fact decisive -- if it does, you have a theorem, not a vacuity; (c) state which binders the result still needs (mine needs Field twice for uniqueness and nothing for inhabitation) so the transfer question is visible rather than assumed. See [[nonvacuity-witness-must-satisfy-the-binders]] and [[witness-site-makes-consequent-free]] for the failure mode this is the complement of.",

      "body": "A RETRACTION PARAGRAPH IS THE LEAST AUDITED PROSE IN A FILE, AND IT CERTIFIES THE LIST IT SITS IN\n\npic-c (AJCR 0092) spent a whole commit (fc9dda7cbe) retracting one fabricated citation from a main-declarations list, wrote \"this is exactly the cited-names-need-check-not-grep failure the workspace keeps filing\", and left a SECOND nonexistent name (instInhabitedDivFamZarZero) three lines above in the same list. The retraction did not trigger a re-check of its own list. Worse, the retraction now reads as an audit of that list, so the next reader trusts it more than before.\n\nThe same paragraph also priced its own blocker in the wrong direction: \"Over.resAlgHom must agree with algebraMap and that is NOT rfl, it needs tower instances I did not build\". The consumer, DivFamZar.mapAlgHom, DEFINES the algebra structure from the map, so the agreement is free at every map -- the retracted declaration was a few lines away, and the theorem the file DID land (mapAlgHom_trivZar) had manufactured the obstruction by carrying [Algebra A A'] + [IsScalarTower] + hphi binders it does not need.\n\nTWO RULES, both cheap:\n1. When you retract a citation, #check EVERY OTHER name in the same list in the same pass. The list is one unit of trust; fixing one entry raises the credibility of the rest without measuring them.\n2. When an attempt stops on \"X = Y is not rfl\", read the DEFINITION of the consumer that needs it before writing the hedge. If the consumer builds the structure from the map (toRingHom.toAlgebra, RingHom.toAlgebra, of_algebraMap_eq), the equation is definitional and the blocker is imaginary. Reaching for a hedge is the moment to open the defining file, not the moment to stop.",

      "body": "A NEW PREDICATE OVER A SHEAF MUST BE PROBED AT THE EMPTY TEST BEFORE ITS REFUTATION IS CALLED A FINDING\n\nPic0ChartMultiIndexInterval.lean defined IndexSeparated f := \"distinct indices never share a value\non a common test\", quantified over ALL tests S, and built a whole file around refuting it at a\ntwo-copy family whose members are injective -- concluding the one-chart V-interval no-go \"does not\npropagate\". The refutation is real and the conclusion drawn from it is not: the project's own\npic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty makes the sheaf a Subsingleton at any empty test, so ALL\nindices share a value there and IndexSeparated f <-> Subsingleton iota for EVERY family. The\n\"witness\" family was decoration; the injectivity of its members did no work; and the \"sharp positive\nform\" carrying the hypothesis was the landed one-chart theorem with extra binders.\n\nThe pattern that hid it: every vacuity sweep we run passes. The definition mentions f. It is not\na Prop-valued constant. Its refutation compiles. jointlyInjective_iff is a true decomposition. What\nwas never asked is whether the quantifier over ALL tests admits a degenerate test that decides the\npredicate independently of f -- and on a big site with a sheaf, the empty scheme always is one, by\nthe sheaf axiom, with no geometry involved. This is the same empty-test triviality already filed as\nsheaf-axiom-gives-empty-test-triviality, arriving from the other side: there it made a priced\nobligation free, here it makes a new hypothesis contentless.\n\nRULE. For any new forall-over-tests predicate on a big-site sheaf: instantiate at the empty test\nFIRST and see whether the predicate is forced (either direction). If it is, the predicate is about\nits index/shape data, not about the maps, and any \"X is not free / X is refuted\" headline built on\nit is about the shape. Cheap probe: state `P f <-> <shape condition>` and try to compile it. Two\nminutes; it inverted this file's entire conclusion.",

      "body": "TWO PROSE DEFECTS, DivisorFamilyDegreeZero.lean.\n\n(1) \"0 is the UNIQUE degree at which the rank clause is vacuous\" (:37-39, :216-218, plus the commit message and the roadmap summary) is false as stated. The clause is vacuous whenever PrimeSpectrum R is EMPTY, i.e. over the trivial ring, and there trivAdapt is certified at EVERY n. Verified: with R = ULift PUnit, all seven fields of IsCertified n close for every n (rankAtStalk_glued := fun p => (IsEmpty.false p).elim), giving DivFamZar C R pi n inhabited at arbitrary n. EXIT=0. import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SerreTwistSections

/-!
# Chart-local finiteness and the twisted extension / vanishing engine (Serre D1–D3)

This file assembles the chart-local inputs of Serre's finiteness theorem
(`lem:sectionGradedModule_fg`, the deep leaf of `Picard/SerreFiniteness.lean`)
along the Option-B ladder.

## D1 — finite sections on affine charts (Stacks 01PC)

For a finitely presented sheaf of modules `F` on a scheme `X` and an affine
open `U`, the section module `Γ(U, F)` is a **finite** `Γ(U, 𝒪)`-module.  The
all-affine form is already proved upstream as
`Scheme.Modules.module_finite_sections_of_isFinitePresentation`
(`Picard/QuotSupportBaseChange.lean`, step 2 of `lem:proper_support_base_change`).
Here it is packaged in the **chart-local** shape the projective endgame consumes:

* `Scheme.Modules.finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom` — the preimage
  `i ⁻¹ᵁ V` of an affine open `V` under an **affine** morphism `i` (in particular
  a closed immersion) is affine (`IsAffineOpen.preimage`) and carries finite
  `F`-sections.  For a projective `X ↪ ℙ` this is finiteness on the standard
  affine charts `Uᵢ = i⁻¹ D₊(xᵢ)`.
* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.finite_sections_chart` — the projective
  specialisation: finiteness of `F`-sections on the preimage of any affine open
  of the ambient projective space.

## D2 / D3 — twisted extension and vanishing ([Hartshorne] II.5.14, Stacks 01PW)

The geometric heart of Serre finiteness is: for the standard chart `Uᵢ = D(xᵢ)`
of a projective `X` with very ample `L`,

* **(D2, extension)** every `t ∈ Γ(Uᵢ, F)` has `xᵢ^N · t` extending to a global
  section of `F ⊗ L^{⊗N}`;
* **(D3, vanishing)** every `s ∈ Γ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗m})` whose restriction to `Uᵢ`
  vanishes has `xᵢ^N · s = 0`.

Both statements reduce — after trivialising `L` on the chart, so that the
coordinate section `xᵢ ∈ Γ(X, L)` becomes an ordinary structure-sheaf section
`g ∈ Γ(Uᵢ, 𝒪)` and `F ⊗ L^{⊗N}` becomes `F` there — to the **qcqs
section-localisation engine** of `Picard/QuotScheme.lean`
(`exists_res_eq_pow_smul_of_isCompact`,
`exists_pow_smul_res_eq_zero_of_isCompact`,
`isLocalizedModule_basicOpen_of_isCompact`; Stacks 01P0).  A **projective**
`π : X ⟶ Spec κ` is proper, hence `X` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated
(`Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.compactSpace`,
`Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.quasiSeparatedSpace`), so the engine runs on the
whole of `X`.

This file proves the **trivialised (structure-sheaf) form** of D2 / D3 in full,
for an arbitrary quasi-coherent sheaf `G` on a quasi-compact quasi-separated
scheme and a global function `g ∈ Γ(X, ⊤)`:

* `Scheme.Modules.isLocalizedModule_globalSection_of_qcqs` — the master
  localisation: `Γ(X, D(g))` is the localisation `Γ(X, G)[1/g]`;
* `Scheme.Modules.exists_global_res_eq_pow_smul` — the extension half (D2);
* `Scheme.Modules.exists_pow_smul_eq_zero_of_res_eq_zero` — the vanishing half
  (D3).

The remaining bridge to the *un-trivialised* D2 / D3 (identifying `Uᵢ` with the
non-vanishing locus of the invertible section `xᵢ` and absorbing the `L^{⊗N}`
twist) is the coordinate/graded trivialisation dictionary of P0.4
(`serreTwistGluedChartIso`, `IsLocallyTrivial`): the invertible-section analogue
of the localisation engine.  It is documented here as the next step of the
ladder and is *not* used by anything downstream yet.

## References

Blueprint: `lem:sectionGradedModule_fg`
(`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).
Source: [Hartshorne] II.5.14, II.5.17; [Nitsure] §1; Stacks tags 01PC
(finite sections on affines), 01PW / 01P0 (section localisation and the twisted
extension/vanishing).

`Γ(X, i ⁻¹ᵁ V)`-module.  The preimage of an affine open under an affine morphism
is affine (`IsAffineOpen.preimage`), so this is the all-affine finiteness
`module_finite_sections_of_isFinitePresentation` read on the standard charts of a
closed embedding `X ↪ ℙ`. -/
theorem finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom {Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsAffineHom i] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] {V : Y.Opens}
    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    Module.Finite Γ(X, i ⁻¹ᵁ V) Γ(F, i ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
  module_finite_sections_of_isFinitePresentation F ⟨_, hV.preimage i⟩

/-- **Master global-section localisation** (Stacks 01P0 / 01PW, structure-sheaf
form).  On a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme `X`, for a quasi-coherent sheaf
`G` and a global function `g ∈ Γ(X, ⊤)`, the basic-open restriction
`Γ(X, G) → Γ(X, D(g))` exhibits `Γ(X, D(g))` as the localisation `Γ(X, G)[1/g]`.

instantiated at the (compact, quasi-separated) open `W = ⊤`; it packages both the
extension (D2, `IsLocalizedModule.surj`) and the vanishing (D3,
`IsLocalizedModule.exists_of_eq`) halves. -/
theorem isLocalizedModule_globalSection_of_qcqs [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (G : X.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] (g : Γ(X, ⊤)) :
    letI : Module Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(G, X.basicOpen g) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(X, X.basicOpen g))
    letI : IsScalarTower Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(X, X.basicOpen g) Γ(G, X.basicOpen g) :=

    IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers g) (restrictBasicOpenₗ G g) := by

    rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_top]; exact isCompact_univ
  have hsep : IsQuasiSeparated ((⊤ : X.Opens) : Set X) := by
    rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_top]; exact isQuasiSeparated_univ
  exact isLocalizedModule_basicOpen_of_isCompact G hW hsep g

extension of `t` off the basic open `D(g)` up to the invertibility factor `g^n`,
the trivialised model of "`xᵢ^N · t` extends to `Γ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗N})`".  The scalar

`Γ(X, ⊤) → Γ(X, D(g))` (the `compHom` module carried in the statement). -/
theorem exists_global_res_eq_pow_smul [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (G : X.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] (g : Γ(X, ⊤)) :
    letI : Module Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(G, X.basicOpen g) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(X, X.basicOpen g))
    ∀ t : Γ(G, X.basicOpen g), ∃ (s : Γ(G, ⊤)) (n : ℕ),
      G.presheaf.map (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le g)).op s = g ^ n • t := by
  letI : Module Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(G, X.basicOpen g) :=
    Module.compHom _ (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(X, X.basicOpen g))
  letI : IsScalarTower Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(X, X.basicOpen g) Γ(G, X.basicOpen g) :=
    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul (fun _ _ => rfl)
  haveI := isLocalizedModule_globalSection_of_qcqs G g

    (restrictBasicOpenₗ G g) t

  have hgn : (g : Γ(X, ⊤)) ^ n = (c : Γ(X, ⊤)) := hn

"`s ∈ Γ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗m})` vanishing on `Uᵢ` has `xᵢ^N · s = 0`"; the scalar action

theorem exists_pow_smul_eq_zero_of_res_eq_zero [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (G : X.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] (g : Γ(X, ⊤)) (s : Γ(G, ⊤))
    (hs : G.presheaf.map (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le g)).op s = 0) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, g ^ n • s = 0 := by

    Module.compHom _ (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(X, X.basicOpen g))
  letI : IsScalarTower Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(X, X.basicOpen g) Γ(G, X.basicOpen g) :=

  rw [hgn]
  exact hc

end Scheme.Modules

/-! ## Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of a projective total space -/

namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith

variable {X S : Scheme.{0}} {π : X ⟶ S} {L : X.Modules}

/-- **A projective total space over a quasi-compact base is quasi-compact.**
`π` projective is proper (`isProper`), hence quasi-compact, and quasi-compact
morphisms lift compactness from a compact target
(`QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace`).  Over `Spec κ` (a compact affine
scheme) this gives `CompactSpace X`, one half of the qcqs hypothesis feeding the
section-localisation engine on `X`. -/
theorem compactSpace (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) [CompactSpace S] : CompactSpace X := by
  haveI := h.isProper
  exact QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace π

/-- **A projective total space over a quasi-separated base is quasi-separated.**
`π` projective is proper (`isProper`), hence separated and so quasi-separated, and
quasi-separated morphisms lift quasi-separatedness from a quasi-separated target
(`quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated`).  Over `Spec κ` (an affine, hence
quasi-separated, scheme) this gives `QuasiSeparatedSpace X`, the second half of
the qcqs hypothesis. -/
theorem quasiSeparatedSpace (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] :
    QuasiSeparatedSpace X := by
  haveI := h.isProper
  exact quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated π

/-- **D1 on the projective charts** (Stacks 01PC).  For a projective `π` carrying
`L`, realised by a closed immersion `i : X ⟶ ℙ(Fin (d+1); S)`, and a finitely
presented `F`, the section module of `F` over the preimage `i ⁻¹ᵁ V` of any affine
open `V` of the ambient projective space is a finite `Γ(X, i ⁻¹ᵁ V)`-module.  In
particular this applies to the standard coordinate charts `Uᵢ = i ⁻¹ᵁ D₊(xᵢ)`,
which are affine because a closed immersion is an affine morphism.  Existential in
the embedding data (`i`, `d`) recorded by `IsProjectiveWith`. -/
theorem finite_sections_chart (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(Fin (d + 1); S)), IsClosedImmersion i ∧
      i ≫ (ℙ(Fin (d + 1); S) ↘ S) = π ∧
      ∀ V : (ℙ(Fin (d + 1); S)).Opens, IsAffineOpen V →
        Module.Finite Γ(X, i ⁻¹ᵁ V) Γ(F, i ⁻¹ᵁ V) := by
  obtain ⟨d, i, hi, hcomp, he⟩ := h
  haveI := hi
  exact ⟨d, i, hi, hcomp, fun V hV =>
    Scheme.Modules.finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom i F hV⟩

/-! ## The section-localisation engine on a projective total space -/

/-- **D2 on the projective total space** ([Hartshorne] II.5.14 (a), structure-sheaf
form).  For a projective `π : X ⟶ S` over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base and a
quasi-coherent sheaf `G` on `X`, every section `t ∈ Γ(X, D(g))` over the basic open of
a global function `g ∈ Γ(X, ⊤)` becomes, after multiplication by a power `g^n`, the
restriction of a **global** section of `G`.  `X` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated
because `π` is proper (`compactSpace`, `quasiSeparatedSpace`), so the qcqs
section-localisation engine `Scheme.Modules.exists_global_res_eq_pow_smul` runs
directly on `X`.  This is the trivialised (`L`-untwisted) extension half of D2 on the
projective total space itself; the scalar action of `g^n` on `Γ(X, D(g))` is through
the restriction `Γ(X, ⊤) → Γ(X, D(g))`. -/
theorem exists_global_res_eq_pow_smul [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) (G : X.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] (g : Γ(X, ⊤)) :
    letI : Module Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(G, X.basicOpen g) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(X, X.basicOpen g))
    ∀ t : Γ(G, X.basicOpen g), ∃ (s : Γ(G, ⊤)) (n : ℕ),
      G.presheaf.map (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le g)).op s = g ^ n • t := by
  haveI := h.compactSpace
  haveI := h.quasiSeparatedSpace
  exact Scheme.Modules.exists_global_res_eq_pow_smul G g

/-- **D3 on the projective total space** ([Hartshorne] II.5.14 (b), structure-sheaf
form).  For a projective `π : X ⟶ S` over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base and a
quasi-coherent sheaf `G` on `X`, a global section `s` of `G` whose restriction to the
basic open `D(g)` of a global function `g ∈ Γ(X, ⊤)` vanishes is annihilated by a power
`g^n`.  As above `X` is qcqs because `π` is proper, so the qcqs vanishing engine
`Scheme.Modules.exists_pow_smul_eq_zero_of_res_eq_zero` runs directly on `X` — the
trivialised (`L`-untwisted) vanishing half of D3 on the projective total space. -/
theorem exists_pow_smul_eq_zero_of_res_eq_zero [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) (G : X.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (g : Γ(X, ⊤)) (s : Γ(G, ⊤))
    (hs : G.presheaf.map (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le g)).op s = 0) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, g ^ n • s = 0 := by
  haveI := h.compactSpace
  haveI := h.quasiSeparatedSpace
  exact Scheme.Modules.exists_pow_smul_eq_zero_of_res_eq_zero G g s hs

end Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveMorphismBasic
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveCoordinateChart
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveSpaceAffineChartIso
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.TwistedProjectiveCoordinates
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineSpace
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.ZariskisMainTheorem

/-!
# Finite-morphism embeddings

This file supplies two pieces of the standard proof that finite morphisms are
projective. Over an affine target, a finite morphism is a closed subscheme of
finite-dimensional affine space. At the other end of the compactification
argument, a proper immersion into projective space is already closed.

The remaining geometric step is to place the affine embedding in a projective
chart and globalize it over the target. These results isolate both sides of
that step without adding a projectivity hypothesis.
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial

noncomputable section

universe u

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective

variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}

/-- A proper morphism that factors through projective space by an immersion is
projective. Properness makes the immersion closed. -/
theorem of_isProper_of_immersion (hpi : IsProper pi) {n : Type u} [Finite n]
    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hi : IsImmersion i)
    (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) : pi.IsProjective := by
  letI : IsImmersion i := hi
  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := hcomp ▸ hpi
  haveI : IsProper i := IsProper.of_comp i (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)
  haveI : IsClosedImmersion i :=
    (IsClosedImmersion.iff_isProper_and_mono (f := i)).mpr
      ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
  exact ⟨n, inferInstance, i, inferInstance, hcomp⟩

end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective

namespace IsFinite

/-- A specified finite module-spanning family in the affine source ring
defines a closed immersion into affine space over the base. This is the
chosen-generator form of `exists_closedImmersion_affineSpace`, used when the
generators on two base charts have already been aligned. -/

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**

    11	/-!
    12	# The standard projective chart ring
    13	
    14	For a finite coordinate type `n`, this file identifies the degree-zero
    15	homogeneous localization of `R[X_none, X_i]` at `X_none` with the polynomial
    16	ring `R[X_i]`. This is the algebraic half of the standard-chart identification
    17	between `ProjectiveSpace.affineChart n S` and affine space over `S`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	set_option autoImplicit false
    21	
    22	open MvPolynomial HomogeneousLocalization
    23	
    24	noncomputable section
    25	
    26	universe u
    27	
    28	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.AffineChartRing
    29	
    30	section
    31	
    32	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    33	variable (n : Type u)
    34	
    35	/-- Every homogeneous coordinate, including the homogenizing coordinate, has
    36	degree one. -/
    37	theorem X_mem_deg_one (i : Option n) :
    38	    (X i : MvPolynomial (Option n) R) ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R 1 :=
    39	  isHomogeneous_X _ _
    40	
    41	/-- The degree-zero part of the homogeneous coordinate ring consists of the
    42	constants. -/
    43	theorem exists_algebraMap_eq_gradeZero
    44	    (c : homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R 0) :
    45	    ∃ r : R, algebraMap R (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R 0) r = c := by
    46	  have hc : (c : MvPolynomial (Option n) R) ∈
    47	      (1 : Submodule R (MvPolynomial (Option n) R)) := by
    48	    rw [← homogeneousSubmodule_zero (σ := Option n) (R := R)]
    49	    exact c.2
    50	  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := Submodule.mem_one.mp hc
    51	  exact ⟨r, Subtype.ext (by simpa using hr)⟩
    52	
    53	/-- The homogeneous coordinate ring is generated over its degree-zero part by
    54	its variables. -/
    55	theorem adjoin_gradeZero_range_X :
    56	    Algebra.adjoin (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R 0)
    57	      (Set.range (X : Option n → MvPolynomial (Option n) R)) = ⊤ := by
    58	  rw [eq_top_iff]
    59	  rintro p -
    60	  have hp : p ∈ Algebra.adjoin R
    61	      (Set.range (X : Option n → MvPolynomial (Option n) R)) := by
    62	    rw [MvPolynomial.adjoin_range_X]
    63	    trivial
    64	  induction hp using Algebra.adjoin_induction with
    65	  | mem q hq => exact Algebra.subset_adjoin hq
    66	  | algebraMap r =>
    67	      exact Subalgebra.algebraMap_mem _
    68	        (⟨algebraMap R (MvPolynomial (Option n) R) r, by
    69	          rw [MvPolynomial.algebraMap_eq]
    70	          exact isHomogeneous_C _ r⟩ : homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R 0)
    71	  | add q₁ q₂ _ _ h₁ h₂ => exact add_mem h₁ h₂
    72	  | mul q₁ q₂ _ _ h₁ h₂ => exact mul_mem h₁ h₂
    73	
    74	variable [GradedAlgebra (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R)]
    75	
    76	/-- The normalized affine coordinate `X_j / X_none`. -/
    77	def chartCoord (j : n) :
    78	    Away (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X none) :=
    79	  Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X_mem_deg_one R n none) 1 (X (some j))
    80	    (by simpa using X_mem_deg_one R n (some j))
    81	
    82	/-- Dehomogenization sends `X_none` to one and every `X_j` to the
    83	corresponding affine variable. -/
    84	def dehomogenize : MvPolynomial (Option n) R →ₐ[R] MvPolynomial n R :=
    85	  MvPolynomial.aeval fun o => o.elim 1 (fun j => X j)
    86	
    87	omit [GradedAlgebra (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R)] in
    88	@[simp]
    89	theorem dehomogenize_X_none : dehomogenize R n (X none) = 1 := by
    90	  simp [dehomogenize]
    91	
    92	omit [GradedAlgebra (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R)] in
    93	@[simp]
    94	theorem dehomogenize_X_some (j : n) : dehomogenize R n (X (some j)) = X j := by
    95	  simp [dehomogenize]
    96	
    97	omit [GradedAlgebra (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R)] in
    98	private theorem isUnit_dehomogenize_X_none :
    99	    IsUnit ((dehomogenize R n).toRingHom (X none)) := by
   100	  have h : (dehomogenize R n).toRingHom (X none) = 1 := by
   101	    change dehomogenize R n (X none) = 1
   102	    exact dehomogenize_X_none R n
   103	  rw [h]
   104	  exact isUnit_one
   105	
   106	/-- The map from affine polynomials to the standard chart ring. -/
   107	def polyToAway : MvPolynomial n R →ₐ[R]
   108	    Away (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X none) :=
   109	  MvPolynomial.aeval (chartCoord R n)
   110	
   111	@[simp]
   112	theorem polyToAway_X (j : n) : polyToAway R n (X j) = chartCoord R n j :=
   113	  MvPolynomial.aeval_X _ _
   114	
   115	/-- Dehomogenization descends from the ordinary localization to its
   116	degree-zero subring. -/
   117	def awayToPoly : Away (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X none) →ₐ[R]
   118	    MvPolynomial n R where
   119	  toRingHom :=
   120	    (Localization.awayLift (dehomogenize R n).toRingHom (X none)
   121	      (isUnit_dehomogenize_X_none R n)).comp
   122	      (algebraMap (Away (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X none))
   123	        (Localization.Away (X none : MvPolynomial (Option n) R)))
   124	  commutes' r := by
   125	    change (Localization.awayLift (dehomogenize R n).toRingHom (X none)
   126	        (isUnit_dehomogenize_X_none R n))
   127	        ((algebraMap R (Away (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X none)) r).val) =
   128	      algebraMap R (MvPolynomial n R) r
   129	    rw [HomogeneousLocalization.algebraMap_val, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq]
   130	    exact (dehomogenize R n).commutes r
   131	
   132	/-- Evaluation of `awayToPoly` on a homogeneous fraction. -/
   133	theorem awayToPoly_mk (a : ℕ) (p : MvPolynomial (Option n) R)
   134	    (hp : p ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R (a • 1)) :
   135	    awayToPoly R n
   136	        (Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X_mem_deg_one R n none) a p hp) =
   137	      dehomogenize R n p := by
   138	  have h1 : (dehomogenize R n).toRingHom (X none) * 1 = 1 := by
   139	    rw [mul_one]
   140	    change dehomogenize R n (X none) = 1
   141	    exact dehomogenize_X_none R n
   142	  have h := Localization.awayLift_mk (A := MvPolynomial n R)
   143	    ((dehomogenize R n).toRingHom) (X none) p 1 h1 a
   144	  exact h.trans (by rw [one_pow, mul_one]; rfl)
   145	
   146	@[simp]
   147	theorem awayToPoly_chartCoord (j : n) :
   148	    awayToPoly R n (chartCoord R n j) = X j :=
   149	  (awayToPoly_mk R n 1 (X (some j))
   150	    (by simpa using X_mem_deg_one R n (some j))).trans
   151	      (dehomogenize_X_some R n j)
   152	
   153	/-- Dehomogenization is a left inverse to the affine-coordinate map. -/
   154	theorem awayToPoly_comp_polyToAway :
   155	    (awayToPoly R n).comp (polyToAway R n) =
   156	      AlgHom.id R (MvPolynomial n R) := by
   157	  apply MvPolynomial.algHom_ext
   158	  intro j
   159	  rw [AlgHom.comp_apply, polyToAway_X, awayToPoly_chartCoord, AlgHom.id_apply]
   160	
   161	/-! ### Surjectivity of the affine-coordinate map -/
   162	
   163	variable [Finite n]
   164	local instance : Fintype n := Fintype.ofFinite n
   165	
   166	/-- Reading the total degree off an exponent vector indexed by `Option n`. -/
   167	private theorem degree_eq {e : Option n → ℕ} {a : ℕ}
   168	    (hae : ∑ l, e l • (1 : ℕ) = a • (1 : ℕ)) :
   169	    e none + ∑ j, e (some j) = a := by
   170	  simpa [Fintype.sum_option] using hae
   171	
   172	omit [Finite n] in
   173	/-- The value of a normalized affine coordinate in the ordinary localization. -/
   174	theorem val_chartCoord (j : n) :
   175	    (chartCoord R n j).val = Localization.mk (X (some j))
   176	      (⟨X none ^ 1, 1, rfl⟩ :
   177	        Submonoid.powers (X none : MvPolynomial (Option n) R)) :=
   178	  rfl
   179	
   180	/-- A spanning homogeneous monomial is the corresponding monomial in the
   181	normalized affine coordinates. -/
   182	private theorem away_mk_prod_eq (a : ℕ) (e : Option n → ℕ)
   183	    (hae : e none + ∑ j, e (some j) = a)
   184	    (H : (∏ l, (X l : MvPolynomial (Option n) R) ^ e l) ∈
   185	      homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R (a • 1)) :
   186	    Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X_mem_deg_one R n none) a
   187	        (∏ l, X l ^ e l) H =
   188	      ∏ j, chartCoord R n j ^ e (some j) := by
   189	  apply (show Function.Injective (algebraMap
   190	      (Away (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X none))
   191	      (Localization.Away (X none : MvPolynomial (Option n) R))) from
   192	    HomogeneousLocalization.val_injective _)
   193	  simp only [map_prod, map_pow, HomogeneousLocalization.algebraMap_apply,
   194	    Away.val_mk, chartCoord, Localization.mk_pow, Localization.mk_prod]
   195	  rw [Fintype.prod_option, Localization.mk_eq_mk_iff, Localization.r_iff_exists]
   196	  refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
   197	  push_cast
   198	  rw [Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum, ← hae, pow_add]
   199	  ring
   200	
   201	/-- Every element of the standard chart ring is a polynomial in the normalized
   202	affine coordinates. -/
   203	theorem polyToAway_surjective : Function.Surjective (polyToAway R n) := by
   204	  intro z
   205	  have hz : z ∈
   206	      (⊤ : Submodule (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R 0)
   207	        (Away (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X none))) := trivial
   208	  rw [← Away.span_mk_prod_pow_eq_top (X_mem_deg_one R n none) X
   209	    (adjoin_gradeZero_range_X R n) (fun _ => 1) (fun l => X_mem_deg_one R n l)] at hz
   210	  induction hz using Submodule.span_induction with
   211	  | mem w hw =>
   212	      obtain ⟨a, e, hae, rfl⟩ := hw
   213	      refine ⟨∏ j, X j ^ e (some j), ?_⟩
   214	      rw [map_prod]
   215	      simp_rw [map_pow, polyToAway_X]
   216	      exact (away_mk_prod_eq R n a e (degree_eq n hae) _).symm
   217	  | zero => exact ⟨0, map_zero _⟩
   218	  | add u v _ _ hu hv =>
   219	      obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := hu
   220	      obtain ⟨q, rfl⟩ := hv
   221	      exact ⟨p + q, map_add _ _ _⟩
   222	  | smul c w _ hw =>
   223	      obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := hw
   224	      obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := exists_algebraMap_eq_gradeZero R n c
   225	      exact ⟨r • p, by rw [map_smul, IsScalarTower.algebraMap_smul]⟩
   226	
   227	omit [Finite n] in
   228	theorem awayToPoly_polyToAway_apply (p : MvPolynomial n R) :
   229	    awayToPoly R n (polyToAway R n p) = p :=
   230	  AlgHom.congr_fun (awayToPoly_comp_polyToAway R n) p
   231	
   232	/-- The affine-coordinate map is also a left inverse to dehomogenization. -/
   233	theorem polyToAway_comp_awayToPoly :
   234	    (polyToAway R n).comp (awayToPoly R n) =
   235	      AlgHom.id R (Away (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X none)) := by
   236	  refine AlgHom.ext fun z => ?_
   237	  obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := polyToAway_surjective R n z
   238	  rw [AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgHom.id_apply, awayToPoly_polyToAway_apply]
   239	
   240	/-- The standard projective chart ring is the polynomial ring on the remaining
   241	homogeneous coordinates. -/
   242	def awayAlgEquiv :
   243	    Away (homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) R) (X none) ≃ₐ[R] MvPolynomial n R :=
   244	  AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom (awayToPoly R n) (polyToAway R n)
   245	    (awayToPoly_comp_polyToAway R n) (polyToAway_comp_awayToPoly R n)
   246	
   247	@[simp]
   248	theorem awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord (j : n) :
   249	    awayAlgEquiv R n (chartCoord R n j) = X j :=
   250	  awayToPoly_chartCoord R n j
   251	
   252	@[simp]
   253	theorem awayAlgEquiv_symm_X (j : n) :
   254	    (awayAlgEquiv R n).symm (X j) = chartCoord R n j :=
   255	  (awayAlgEquiv R n).symm_apply_eq.mpr (awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord R n j).symm
   256	
   257	end

   259	end AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.AffineChartRing

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveSpace

/-!
# The standard affine chart of relative projective space

This file constructs the standard chart `D_+(X_none)` of
`P(Option n; S)` as the base change of Mathlib's affine chart
`Proj.awayι`. The identification of its chart ring with a polynomial ring,
and hence of this scheme with `A(n; S)`, is deliberately a separate algebraic
step.
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial

noncomputable section

universe u

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace ProjectiveSpace

variable (n : Type u) (S : Scheme.{u})

local notation3 "P[" n "]" =>
  homogeneousSubmodule (Option n) (ULift ℤ)

/-- The distinguished homogenizing coordinate has degree one. -/
private lemma X_none_mem_deg_one :
    (X none : MvPolynomial (Option n) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ∈ P[n] 1 :=
  isHomogeneous_X _ _

/-- The standard `D_+(X_none)` chart of relative projective space. It is the
pullback of the corresponding affine open of the integral `Proj` model. -/
def affineChart : Scheme.{u} :=
  pullback (toProjInt (Option n) S)
    (Proj.awayι P[n] (X none) (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one)

namespace affineChart

/-- The inclusion of the standard chart into relative projective space. -/
def incl : affineChart n S ⟶ ℙ(Option n; S) :=
  pullback.fst (toProjInt (Option n) S)
    (Proj.awayι P[n] (X none) (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one)

instance : IsOpenImmersion (incl n S) := by
  dsimp [incl]
  exact MorphismProperty.pullback_fst _ _
    (Proj.instIsOpenImmersionAwayι P[n] (X none)
      (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one)

/-- The chart inclusion followed by the integral-model projection is the
other pullback projection followed by `Proj.awayι`. -/
@[reassoc]
theorem incl_toProjInt :
    incl n S ≫ toProjInt (Option n) S =
      pullback.snd (toProjInt (Option n) S)
          (Proj.awayι P[n] (X none) (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one) ≫
        Proj.awayι P[n] (X none) (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one :=
  pullback.condition

instance : (affineChart n S).CanonicallyOver S where
  hom := incl n S ≫ (ℙ(Option n; S) ↘ S)

@[simp]
theorem over_eq : affineChart n S ↘ S = incl n S ≫ (ℙ(Option n; S) ↘ S) :=
  rfl

/-- The chart is exactly the inverse image of `D_+(X_none)` in the integral
model. -/
theorem opensRange_incl :
    (incl n S).opensRange =
      toProjInt (Option n) S ⁻¹ᵁ
        Proj.basicOpen P[n] (X none) := by
  change (pullback.fst (toProjInt (Option n) S)
      (Proj.awayι P[n] (X none) (X_none_mem_deg_one n) Nat.zero_lt_one)).opensRange = _
  rw [Scheme.Hom.opensRange_pullbackFst, Proj.opensRange_awayι]

end affineChart

end ProjectiveSpace

end AlgebraicGeometry
